blocks.text: The server endpoints are abstract contracts viewed from the client. They expose stable identity, explicit revisions, device-appropriate artwork candidates, and idempotent commands. They do not leak recommendation-service topology into components. Obsolete reads and media work are cancellable when route, profile, or intent changes. Once a destructive command may have reached the service, the action coordinator retains its identity until an idempotent retry, response, or refresh confirms the outcome.

blocks.code:
DELETE /ui/home/rows/continue-watching/items/title_b
Idempotency-Key: remove-2bd6
If-Match: "cw-p7-21"

200 OK
{
  "rowRevision": 22,
  "removedTitleId": "title_b"
}

409 Conflict
{
  "code": "ROW_REVISION_CHANGED",
  "currentRowRevision": 22,
  "message": "The row changed on another device."
}

blocks.title: Contract choices
rows: A stale response is ignored or triggers a focused refetch.
A returning view can validate cached data cheaply.
A missing cache simply receives a complete payload.
A lost response can be retried without removing another item.
The same key resolves to the same command outcome.
The client fetches or accepts the newer row and explains the conflict.
Obsolete row and artwork work releases resources.
A dispatched removal stays tracked by idempotency key instead of being mistaken for a cancelled product action.
The payload can avoid obviously unsuitable assets.
The UI still has a safe generic candidate fallback.

blocks.text: Authentication failure transitions the feature to a signed-out or profile-unavailable state instead of retrying forever. A revision conflict is recoverable and distinct from validation or permission failure. Network uncertainty keeps the base row visible and labels the command outcome as unknown until an idempotent retry or refresh resolves it. Invalid individual title records are quarantined so one malformed card does not remove the entire row. The client records contract violations without rendering raw server details to the member.

blocks.title: Avoid endpoint-shaped components
blocks.text: A card should receive a render-ready title identity and callbacks. It should not know URLs, ETags, idempotency keys, or revision conflict codes.
